Q: do layering of spring packages really matters , why cant i just use controller and entity classes in same package A:

Using a single package eliminates all benefits of packaged. You’re really asking “why use packages “, which you can search for.

Q: How to draw a diagonal line with mark_rule that stretches to infinity in Altair A:

Update: To create an identity line that is robust to both zooming and panning of interactive charts, you can use an expression that re-computes the scale of where to draw the line as the axis domains change:

line = alt.Chart().mark_rule().encode(
    x=alt.value(alt.expr("scale('x', domain('x')[0])")),
    y=alt.value(alt.expr("scale('y', domain('x')[0])")),
    x2=alt.value(alt.expr("scale('x', domain('x')[1])")),
    y2=alt.value(alt.expr("scale('y', domain('x')[1])")),
)

Yes, by using alt.value you can anchor the line to a pixel value rather than a value of the data axis. So even if you zoom out and the axis extent change, the line will span the same pixel distance. You can either hardcode the heigth/width of the chart or use the special signals for this like so:

import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data

source = data.cars.url

points = alt.Chart(source).mark_circle(size=60).encode(
    x='Horsepower:Q',
    y='Miles_per_Gallon:Q',
)

line_black = alt.Chart().mark_rule().encode(
    x=alt.value('width'),
    x2=alt.value(0),
    y2=alt.value(0),
    y=alt.value('height')
)

line_red = alt.Chart().mark_rule(color='red').encode(
    x=alt.value(0),
    x2=alt.value('width'),
    y=alt.value('height'),
    y2=alt.value(0)
)


(points + line_black + line_red).interactive()

Zoomed out:

The above would create the line x=y only if the x and y scale's domain spans the same range. If that is not the case (like for the data above), you have two options:

1. Manually change the scale domain to be the same

We can set the y=axis to have the same max as the xaxis:

points = alt.Chart(source).mark_circle(size=60).encode(
    x='Horsepower:Q',
    y=alt.Y('Miles_per_Gallon:Q').scale(domainMax=240),
)

2. Compute the lines as the ratio of the original domains

I'm not sure if there is a way to automatically find the max value of the y and x domain, but that would make this more robust (maybe look around in the Vega-Lite issue tracker or ask there). For now, I just plug in the values manually:

line_black = alt.Chart().mark_rule().encode(
    x=alt.value(0),
    y=alt.value(0),
    x2=alt.value(alt.expr('width * 50/240')),
    y2=alt.value('height'),
)

line_red = alt.Chart().mark_rule(color='red').encode(
    x=alt.value(0),
    y=alt.value('height'),
    x2=alt.value(alt.expr('width * 50/240')),
    y2=alt.value(0),
)

It would be nice to have this in the docs, so feel free to add a PR to the rule page if you wish https://altair-viz.github.io/user_guide/marks/rule.html#width-height-spanning-rules. Issue here https://github.com/altair-viz/altair/issues/3317

Q: Using a Named Range to identify worksheets to use a SUMIFS on a to add an array of data A:

this is how you can stack multiple INDIRECTs:

=REDUCE(TOCOL(,1), TOCOL(B4:B24, 1), LAMBDA(x, y, VSTACK(x, INDIRECT(y&"!A6:F100"))))

then just do simple query or whatever you need:

=LET(r, REDUCE(TOCOL(,1), TOCOL(B4:B24, 1), LAMBDA(x, y, VSTACK(x, INDIRECT(y&"!A6:F100")))),
 QUERY(QUERY(r, "select Col1,sum(Col6) where Col4='"&B2&"' group by Col1"), "offset 1", ))

you can even get a list of sheet names: how to get List of GID numbers and List of Sheet Names in Google Sheets?
